chunks: Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Nuh (peace be upon him) used to say that whenever it was morning, so he was named due to that as a grateful servant.
And he (peace be upon him) said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Whoever is truthful with Allah, he is rescued.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of being truthful with God (sadaq Allah) in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi underscores the transformative power of consistent morning dhikr, linking the Prophet Nuh’s (peace be upon him) daily practice to his designation as a 'grateful servant' (Abdun Shakur). It further connects this gratitude to the Prophetic principle of 'sadaq Allah' (sincerity/truthfulness with God), establishing a direct causal link between spiritual integrity and ultimate salvation (naja), a concept deeply valued in Shia theological discourse on the relationship between faith and action.
